Good holiday Monday afternoon! Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 662 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Bryan McBournie for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Trump's diesel deal poses Putin problem
 
Photo illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Photo: Suzanne Plunkett/Getty Images

Republicans already saddled with Trump's unpopular policies in the midterms now face another awkward choice: whether to back his diesel deal with a dictator many of them despise, Axios' Andrew Pantazi reports.

The big picture: The deal — which calls for Russia to supply diesel to U.S. and global markets — packs some of the GOP's biggest liabilities into one decision: the Iran war's economic fallout, the party's split over Russia, and a president determined to make the election about himself.

  • Energy analysts also doubt it will do much for diesel prices, which average $6.27 a gallon today, up 71% from a year earlier.

😡 Several Republican lawmakers criticized the deal over the weekend.

  • Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) told NBC News' "Meet the Press" that it may violate a law requiring the White House to notify Congress before lifting sanctions.
  • Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-Pa.) vowed to force a House vote blocking the oil purchases.

Yes, but: Some Republicans, like Florida Rep. Anna Paulina Luna and Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, backed the arrangement.

The White House pushed back on criticism of Trump's record. White House spokesman Davis Ingle told Axios: "President Trump has consistently proven his doubters wrong."

  • A senior administration official said Trump is "laser-focused on bringing down costs, whether it's diesel with the Russians or importing Argentine beef. Some people might not like it, but he's thinking of what Americans are paying and what he can do about it."

2. 🤖 Meta unveils new frontier-class AI models
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

New this afternoon: Meta launched a new family of AI models that it says can compete at the technological frontier, Axios' Ina Fried reports.

  • That would mark a big milestone in its effort to catch up with rivals OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.

👨🏽‍💻 The company says its new Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full models deliver state-of-the-art performance on a range of tasks.

  • Meta Superintelligence Labs head Alexandr Wang tells Axios: "These are true frontier models, competitive with the best models in the world, and are particularly state-of-the-art on personal and professional agentic work."

🧠 Zoom in: Meta is emphasizing two of the models' capabilities, "Active Memory" and "Active Focus."

  • Active Memory allows AI to retain important information about users across conversations and retrieve it as needed.
  • Active Focus keeps AI agents working toward a goal, using different approaches and adapting to new information.

👀 What we're watching: Whether Meta's claimed performance holds up in independent testing.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Homeland Security Investigations police remove documents from Rep. Ilhan Omar's home in D.C. this morning. Photo: Andrew Leyden/Getty Images
  1. 🔎 Federal agents conducted a pre-dawn search at the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) in Northeast D.C. today as part of an ongoing immigration probe, a Justice Department spokesperson told Axios. Omar, who was born in Somalia and calls herself "the first African refugee to become a Member of Congress," tweeted: "I will not be silenced." House Democratic leaders called the raid, 22 days before midterms, "deeply disturbing." Go deeper.
  2. 🇮🇷 British Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the U.K. House of Commons that Iran's Revolutionary Guard was "almost certainly" behind the suspected plot to attack an airbase where U.S. bombers were stationed. More from Barak Ravid.
  3. 🏦 Stanford University's Robert E. Hall and Columbia University's Michael Woodford won the Nobel Prize in economics for research that reshaped how policymakers steady the economy. More from Courtenay Brown.
  4. ☕️ Starbucks denied rumors that it's considering acquiring Chipotle, CNBC reports. The coffee chain's stock is up slightly today, while Chipotle shares are falling. Go deeper.
 
 
4. 🐶 1 fun thing: Mayor bud
 
Photo: Courtesy of Annie Morris

Grandview, Ohio, residents recently picked the city's first "dog mayor," Axios Columbus' Andrew King reports.

🦮 "Grandview girl" Tater was crowned winner of the inaugural election Friday in the neighborhood just outside Columbus.

  • She was sworn in and gave an acceptance speech on the spot.

🐿️ Among Tater's campaign promises: more biscuits, a longer dog swimming season, and a close watch on the area's squirrel population.
